reason: The current goal is to build insulated outgoing nerve routes, so pairing motor fibers with insulating cells seems directly relevant.
expectation: I expect insulated motor nerve fibers, though I don't yet know how they will connect to the arm.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the eyes to sensory nerves also fits the chapter, but the outgoing nerve goal comes first.

effect: The motor nerves are built, and the new goal is to connect sight to muscle commands.
reaction: The segmented wrapping and support-cell role made the construction clearer.
reason: Eyes and sensory nerves seem like the first step toward connecting sight to movement.
expectation: I expect a visual sensory route, though it may still need a central connection before it can guide the muscles.

alternatives.reason: Attaching motor nerves to the arm also seems necessary, but I want to establish the sight route first.

effect: The eyes and sensory nerves now form a visual information route that can connect to the central nervous system.
reaction: The change from light rays to a nerve signal is clear, though the result is brief.
reason: Connecting the visual route to the central nervous system seems like the next step toward linking sight to muscle commands.
expectation: I expect the central nervous system to receive visual information, though the motor connection may still need to be added.

alternatives.reason: The motor nerves also need to connect to the arm, but I want to complete the visual route first.

effect: The visual route now reaches the brain and identifies the glass as a target; the arm still needs a motor connection.
reaction: The distinction between seeing a target and supplying force is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should connect the outgoing nerves to the arm.
expectation: I expect the motor nerves to connect to the arm’s muscles, though the connection to the seeing control system may still be needed.

effect: The motor nerves now reach the arm muscles, leaving the seeing control system to be connected.
reaction: The branching signal arrows make the outgoing route clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should link visual information to the nerve-connected arm.
expectation: I expect a system that can direct the arm toward the seen target; position feedback may still need to be added.

effect: The visual and motor routes are connected, and the remaining goal is to return information about arm position.
reaction: The incoming and outgoing arrows make the connection clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the stretch receptors appear to provide the position feedback the goal calls for.
expectation: I expect the arm to gain a sensory route that reports its position to the central nervous system.

effect: The arm now has a returning sensory route, completing the position-feedback goal and the chapter.
reaction: The eyes-closed inset makes the value of position feedback easy to grasp.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding position feedback was most worthwhile: the eyes-closed example connects the sensors to a familiar experience.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting motor nerves to the arm felt like a brief, predictable assembly step, though the branching arrows clarified the route.

surprise.text: The support cells wrapping motor fibers in separate segments clarified that nerves contain more than neurons.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless. The compatible options made the pairings clear, though several later steps offered only one combination.

continue.text: I would continue: connecting sight, muscle commands and position feedback made me curious about how the assembled arm will act.
